sentences.text: Sulcavis is an extinct genus of enantiornithean birds, a diverse group belonging to the parent family Bohaiornithidae.
This genus is unique among enantiornithes for possessing enlarged teeth with internal grooves, a feature reflected in its name, which combines Latin words for 'groove' and 'bird'.
These robust, grooved teeth likely helped the animal withstand harder food items.
Sulcavis holds the distinction of being the first bird species discovered to have ornamented tooth enamel.
The species name 'geeorum' honors the Gee family for their significant contributions to Mesozoic bird research.
The genus was formally described on January 9, 2013, by a team including Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor and colleagues.
The holotype specimen, found near the town of Lamadong in Liaoning Province, China, was discovered within the Yixian Formation as part of the Jehol Biota.
This fossil was later prepared by Maureen Walsh at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.
Sulcavis is a monotypic extinct genus that lived in what is now China during the Early Cretaceous period.
While one estimate places fossils in rocks dated between 121 and 125 million years ago, another study suggests a time range from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
